subject: SummitBio — deployment fit follow-up: dedicated sizing & concurrency
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lopez <aaron.lopez@summitbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 21:05:00 +0000
Subject: SummitBio kickoff — deployment fit recap & clarifying asks

Hi Aaron,

Thanks again for the call today — good overview of SummitBio's productization timeline and the gateway use-case. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can lock a tight dedicated-capacity recommendation:

What we heard (short):
- Primary need: low-latency clinical summarization and entity extraction for batch+real-time web requests.
- Target SLA: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for single-request path, with bursts during morning and evenings.
- Data posture: HIPAA-adjacent, want private VPC option but will consider Dedicated w/ encryption and audit logs.

Questions for sizing (can you confirm these in the attached token spreadsheet?):
1) Typical TPS pattern: sustained vs peak. On the call you mentioned ~80 TPS sustained and spikes to ~220 TPS — is that correct?
2) Token mix: average prompt tokens vs average response tokens (spreadsheet attached; please fill column B/C).
3) Concurrency model: are calls single-shot calls routed directly, or do you expect long-running multi-turn sessions with KV cache reuse?

Preliminary Redwood guidance (to align expectations):
- For the shape you described, we typically recommend H100-backed Dedicated pools where latency and cache reuse are critical. H100s give better single-request latency for larger models; A100 can be a cost-effective fallback if latency is less strict.
- Example sizing (ballpark): 4x H100 nodes with continuous batching enabled covers ~100–150 sustained TPS for 2k token-per-request profiles; burst capacity or autoscale handles spikes to ~300 TPS.

Next steps I propose:
- Aaron: update the attached token-profile spreadsheet with the last 7 days of traffic (or a representative sample).
- Karthik + Ben: we'll produce a short Dedicated vs Private cost/latency comparison and a specific SKU mix recommendation.
- Quick follow-up call: 30 minutes next week to review the filled spreadsheet and proposed SKU mix.

I've attached a token-profile workbook and our v2 SKU matrix for reference. If you prefer Private from a compliance viewpoint, mention that now and we'll include VPC-onboarding steps and an on-prem checklist in the follow-up.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0162

Attachments: SummitBio_token_profile_20270629.xlsx (spreadsheet to populate), Redwood_dedicated_sku_matrix_v2.pdf (reference)

From: Aaron Lopez <aaron.lopez@summitbio.com>

Cc: contracts@summitbio.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 01:38:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SummitBio kickoff — deployment fit recap & clarifying asks

Kimberly — thanks for the recap and the clear ask.

Quick answers:
- TPS: yes, the numbers on the call are correct. Our observed production baseline is ~75–90 TPS during steady-state (US mornings are higher) and we've seen peaks around 210–240 TPS during scheduled batch runs and product releases.
- Token mix: I'll attach a small CSV export with last week's traffic — average prompt ~180 tokens, average model response ~140 tokens, but some outliers up to 2,500 tokens for full report generation.
- Concurrency: majority of calls are single-shot (stateless), but we have a small set of long-running sessions for internal analysts that would benefit from KV cache reuse. The KV sessions are ~5% of total requests.

Compliance: SummitBio prefers VPC deployment because of our data handling guidelines; however, we'd be open to a Dedicated-managed solution if you can outline the VPC-equivalent controls (KMS, audit logs, private peering).

I'll attach: summit_token_sample_20270623-29.csv. Contracts is looped to flag any procurement items early.

Can you also include a short estimate for cost (monthly) for: 1) Dedicated H100 pool sized for the numbers above, and 2) Private VPC deployment (assume identical throughput but with MTL encryption and extra onboarding).

Thanks,
Aaron
Senior Product Manager, SummitBio
aaron.lopez@summitbio.com

Attachment: summit_token_sample_20270623-29.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SummitBio kickoff — deployment fit recap & clarifying asks

Looping in a quick internal checklist and a proposed approach before we respond to Aaron:

Internal checklist (short):
- Confirm model size and family SummitBio plans to run (Llama2-70B, Mistral, or a fine-tuned 30B?). This changes kernel selection and memory footprint.
- Decide preferred GPU flavor mapping: H100 recommended for 70B LLMs (better latency, lower per-token p99) vs A100 for mid-size models (cost-efficient for 30–40B).
- Autoscale policy recommendation: base pool sized for 90 TPS sustained, burst policy to add 2x nodes when 5-min avg > 120 TPS.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for the 5% long-running sessions; treat them as session-affinity routes.

Sizing proposal (draft numbers):
- Assumptions: avg tokens per request = 320 (prompt+resp), tokens/sec per H100 node w/ continuous batching = ~12k tokens/sec (model dependent).
- To cover 90 TPS * 320 tokens = 28.8k tokens/sec sustained -> ~3 H100 nodes baseline.
- For 220 TPS peak = 70.4k tokens/sec -> add 6 H100 nodes (autoscale to 9 nodes total).
- If workload runs on 30–40B model family, similar throughput can be achieved with 4–6 A100 nodes (cheaper, higher latency).

Action items:
- Karthik: produce a 1-page Dedicated vs Private bulleted comparison with estimated monthly $ ranges for H100 and A100 mixes.
- Kim: propose 2x follow-up slots this week (I'll be on both).

I'll draft the cost ranges and attach a quick node-count calc later today.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Aaron, thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV — that's exactly what we need. Next steps from our side:

1) We'll run the token sample through a quick throughput model and send a short memo with two scenarios: (A) H100-dominant Dedicated pool (latency-optimized) and (B) A100-mix Dedicated (cost-optimized). That memo will include node counts, expected steady-state vs peak capacity, and a monthly cost band.
2) If you prefer Private/VPC, we'll append the VPC onboarding steps and an estimated onboarding timeline (+ security checklist).
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min call to review scenarios — available Thu 07:00–09:00 PDT or Fri 15:00–17:00 PDT. Let me know what works and we'll lock the invite.

Ben will send the internal node-count calc and Karthik will produce the Dedicated vs Private one-pager. Expect our memo + preliminary pricing by EOD tomorrow.

If Contracts wants an early procurement note, we can include a redline-ready SOW stub in that package.

Appreciate the collaboration — we'll aim to keep the recommendation tight so your engineering team can decide quickly.

Best,
